p.i: Extarent hominum luce fruentium, Omnes unius hipectore Guisii Spirabant furiis matribus edita, Plectenda foret ut perdita Gallia Fax, quæ dum placido fouit eum sinu Externum, nimium triftia retulit Eheu hospitij præmia candidi.

Natos namque tuos, Gallia, compulit Durus dulce solum linquere patrium: Urbes cæde, domos ignibus, arvaque Luctu tristifico non semel obruens: Et legem statuens legibus irritis Nil non arbitrio figere proprio, Quo Gallos premeret Bætica sub iuga, Et regi fieret rex dominans suo: Romanaq; lupa captus amoribus, Ludebat simulans callidus artifex Mentes simplicium: Nursius ut vafer Bellacis Marii miles, Ibericos Olim per populos numina mentiens Dianæ specie quadrupedis vaga.

Christi membra sequens & varie secans, Fecit, barbaries ut fera Cæsarum Sit laudata, velut summa benignitas. Testis Parrhisiæ nox truculentiæ Heroum caluit frigida quæ nece. Nox signata pio sanguine: quem Deus Fumantem aspiciens luminibus pijs,

page.notes: The page number may be 50 or 59; the last digit is a worn old-style figure. Long s is transcribed as s throughout. Some words are uncertain: "hipectore" (the ct ligature is read as ct), "Bætica" (ligature assumed), "Parrhisiæ" and "truculentiæ" (ligatures read as æ). Faint show-through of the facing page appears in the right margin and is not transcribed.
